records.question: According to the Introduction, what criteria define Bleaching Alert Level 2 in the Coral Reef Watch-Bleaching Alert System (CRW-BAS)?
records.ground_truth_answer: Bleaching Alert Level 2 is defined as HotSpot ≥ 1 °C and DHW ≥ 8.
ground_truth_chunks: One "Degree Heating Week" (DHW) corresponds to temperatures 1 °C above the maximum monthly mean SST for 7 days. DHW 2 is the same as DHW 1 but for 14 days, or temperatures 2 °C above the maximum monthly mean SST for 7 days, and so on.

Based on cumulative thermal stress, a bleaching warning system was developed: No Stress (HotSpot ≤ 0 °C), Bleaching Watch (0 °C < HotSpot < 1 °C), Bleaching Warning (HotSpot ≥ 1 °C and 0 < DHW < 4), Bleaching Alert Level 1 (HotSpot ≥ 1 °C and 4 ≤ DHW < 8), and Bleaching Alert Level 2 (HotSpot ≥ 1 °C and DHW ≥ 8).

records.question: What were the two locations where the shaded/not-shaded experiments were conducted in the Methods section?
records.ground_truth_answer: An outdoor shaded/notshaded aquarium experiment near reef-flat pools in the National Park of American Samoa on Ofu Island, and a shaded/not-shaded platform experiment in a reef pool in Tutuila.
ground_truth_chunks: A shaded/notshaded aquarium experiment was set-up outdoors, under natural sunlight, near some reef-flat pools in the National Park of American Samoa on Ofu Island.

Also, a shaded/not-shaded platform experiment was carried out in a reef pool in Tutuila in which corals have shown repeated annual summer bleaching for several years [\(Fenner and](#page-10-9) [Heron, 2008](#page-10-9)).

records.question: What instruments were used to measure PAR and UV radiation?
records.ground_truth_answer: PAR was measured with an underwater spherical quantum sensor and a light meter (LiCor*; LI-193SA, LI-250A). UV radiation was measured with a UV radiation sensor and datalogging radiometer (Solar Light*; PMA 2104, PMA 2100) that detected biologically weighted UV in the 280 to 370 nm range.
ground_truth_chunks: Irradiance was measured with an underwater spherical quantum sensor, and light meter, (LiCor\*; LI-193SA, LI-250A) for PAR, and a UV radiation sensor, and datalogging radiometer (Solar Light\*; PMA 2104, PMA 2100), that detected biologically weighted UV, also called "sunburning" UV radiation, in the 280 to 370 nm range following closely the erythema action spectrum (Appendix, Fig. A3).
The UV sensor's peak relative spectral response was between 280 and 300 nm.

records.question: In the Ofu experiment, which shading level (50% or 75%) offered better protection against bleaching?
